ledger.claim_text: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is buried beneath up to 7,500 feet (2,300 meters) of alpine rock, making it the deepest and longest railway tunnel ever constructed at 57.1 km (35.5 miles).
ledger.source_title: AlpTransit Gotthard AG Official Technical Dossier / Swiss Federal Office of Transport
ledger.publisher: Swiss Federal Office of Transport (FOT) / AlpTransit Gotthard AG
ledger.supporting_excerpt_or_notes: Maximum rock overburden reaches 2,300 meters (7,545 ft) beneath Mount Piz Vatgira, setting the world record for railway tunnel depth and length (57.104 km for the western tube).

ledger.claim_text: The Gotthard Base Tunnel measures 57 kilometers (35 miles) in length, bisects 80 distinct rock formations, and required 17 years of continuous construction from 1999 to official opening in 2016.
ledger.source_title: Geology of the Gotthard Base Tunnel: Swiss Journal of Geosciences
ledger.supporting_excerpt_or_notes: The alignment penetrates 80 distinct geological formations ranging from hard granite to treacherous sugar-grained dolomite over 17 years of construction.

ledger.claim_text: Four colossal Herrenknecht Gripper Tunnel Boring Machines excavated 28.2 million metric tons of rock, equivalent to five times the mass of the Great Pyramid of Giza.
ledger.source_title: Herrenknecht AG Gotthard Project Fact Sheet & AlpTransit Excavation Ledger
ledger.supporting_excerpt_or_notes: Total excavated material was 28.2 million tons (13.3 million cubic meters), which is roughly five times the bulk volume of the Great Pyramid of Khufu at Giza (approx. 2.6 million cubic meters).

ledger.claim_text: Virgin rock temperatures deep within the Gotthard massif reached 46°C (115°F), requiring extensive industrial refrigeration and chilled ventilation air to maintain habitable miner temperatures below 28°C.
ledger.source_title: Geothermal and Ventilation Challenges in the Gotthard Base Tunnel: Tunneling and Underground Space Technology
ledger.publisher: Elsevier / International Tunnelling and Underground Space Association
ledger.supporting_excerpt_or_notes: Virgin rock temperature peaked at 46°C (114.8°F). An elaborate refrigeration and cold water heat-exchange system was required to maintain working temperatures within legal Swiss labor limits (28°C).

ledger.claim_text: Overburden pressure caused squeezing rock to deform tunnel diameter inward by up to 80 cm (2.6 feet), solved by deformable sliding steel yielding arches that absorbed rock pressure without collapsing.
ledger.source_title: Kovari, K. (ETH Zurich) - Overcoming Squeezing Rock in the Gotthard Base Tunnel
ledger.publisher: ETH Zurich Institute for Geotechnical Engineering
ledger.supporting_excerpt_or_notes: In the Tavetsch section, crushing pressures induced radial convergence over 70-80 cm. Flexible steel TH yielding arches slipped under controlled friction to avoid catastrophic structural buckle.

ledger.claim_text: When drill heads met on October 15, 2010 after 28 miles of subterranean drilling from northern and southern portals, laser-guided geodetic alignment deviation was under one centimeter (8 mm horizontal, 1 mm vertical).
ledger.source_title: Swiss Federal Office of Topography (swisstopo) - The Geodetic Precision of the Gotthard Breakthrough
ledger.publisher: Federal Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport (DDPS) / swisstopo
ledger.supporting_excerpt_or_notes: The historic breakthrough between Sedrun and Faido on October 15, 2010 recorded a lateral deviation of only 8 centimeters over 30 kilometers, with laser vertical deviation of less than 1 centimeter.

ledger.claim_text: High-speed passenger trains traverse the single-track tubes at 250 km/h (155 mph), pushing an intense aerodynamic air piston wave dissipated via 176 cross-passages spaced every 325 meters.
ledger.source_title: Aerodynamics and Ventilation in Very Long High-Speed Rail Tunnels: SBB CFF FFS Technical Dossier
ledger.supporting_excerpt_or_notes: Single-tube design creates piston effect at 250 km/h (155 mph); side cross-passages equipped with heavy aerodynamic blast doors every 325 meters equalize pressure and provide escape routes.

ledger.claim_text: The Gotthard Base Tunnel establishes a flat rail corridor directly through the Alps at near sea-level gradient, cutting Zurich to Milan transit time and transforming European trans-alpine freight.
ledger.source_title: European Commission Mobility and Transport - Trans-European Transport Network (TEN-T) Rhine-Alpine Corridor
ledger.publisher: European Commission Directorate-General for Mobility and Transport
ledger.supporting_excerpt_or_notes: The flat railway through the Alps eliminates steep alpine climbing grades for freight and reduces passenger transit between Zurich and Milan by up to 60 minutes.
